approach: Root cause: refusing_check (crates/athena-core/src/reading/checks.rs:520-551) is an ordered list of step! checks. None compares the request's explicit parts with the reading's deliverables and criteria, and no rule says an explicit part stays in scope unless the request defers it, so a reading that moves part (3) to out_of_scope is accepted (jobs 20261029-084645-sza7, 20261029-110953-bw7k; failed attempt 20261030-060839-1njk). Fix: check_request_parts as the last step!, so every existing refusal keeps its check name. The design of the earlier rounds stands: a shared request_own_lines filter factored out of plain_request_prose; Enumerated and Bullet parts; distinctive-stem coverage; clause-scoped criterion negation; request-side deferral by marker citation; the person's corrections as request-side text through a corrections parameter of refusing_check; enforcement by code only. This round answers three findings. (F1) The corpus test the_wrapper_agrees_with_refusing_check_on_every_case (refusal_corpus.rs:2800-2823) calls check_reading_acceptance, which has no corrections, so a correction case would disagree with run. A second public wrapper check_reading_acceptance_with_corrections(reading, request, corrections, attempt, referenced, repo_files) calls refusing_check with the corrections; check_reading_acceptance keeps its signature and passes an empty slice; the test compares run(&c) with the new wrapper; a new test pins that the corrections-less wrapper refuses the deferring-correction case; the refusing_check doc sentence 'Order, short-circuit and error text are those of the gate' is reworded to name both wrappers. (F2) queued_work (steward.rs:405-431) calls check_reading_text(latest, &request.text) with no corrections, so a reading accepted after 'athena correct' with 'leave (3) for a follow-up' would silently leave the drain queue until a person runs athena go (steward.rs:402; drain.rs:127-129). Fix: add check_reading_text_with_corrections(reading, request, corrections) in replay.rs (check_reading_text delegates with an empty slice), call it from queued_work with the texts of the job's stored corrections (job.corrections, ordered by reading number, as correct builds its history at reading.rs:1402-1414), add steward.rs to the deliverables, and add a steward test that a corrected, deferring reading stays queued and the same reading without the correction does not. athena check-reading (athena-cli main.rs:683-715) takes only a request file and a reading file and is not a deliverable, so the producer-loop replay still runs without corrections: that is a stated limit and a counted artifact. (F3) run/pin.rs:163-164 (reread_after_configuration_change) builds history with every correction None, so read_once passes no corrections on that path and the reader does not see them either. This is named as a stated limit in the doc comment, CHANGELOG and the report, with the follow-up 'pass stored corrections on the re-read after a configuration change'; it is not described as passing the corrections, and pin.rs is not edited (changing what the reader is shown there is a larger change than this job).

decisions.choice: Placement, retries, corrections and the two gate wrappers. step!(check_request_parts(reading, request)); is the last step! in refusing_check, after check_reading_references (checks.rs:549); it is Ok when capability is none or question is some (as check_governance_coverage). refusing_check's signature becomes (reading, request, corrections: &[String], attempt, referenced, repo_files). Directly before the step: let request = &request_with_retried_parts(request, corrections, attempt); (new fn in topics.rs) returning the retried job's attempt.request, a blank line, the current request, then one line per correction (attempt.corrections first, then the current ones), each USER_CORRECTION_PREFIX ('User correction (data, not a part): ') plus the text with newlines turned to spaces. check_reading_acceptance (checks.rs:492) keeps its signature, calls refusing_check directly with an empty corrections slice, and its body still holds no 'check_' text (corpus no_check_bypasses_refusing_check, refusal_corpus.rs:3209-3220). NEW (F1): pub fn check_reading_acceptance_with_corrections(reading, request, corrections, attempt, referenced, repo_files) -> Result<()>, placed after check_reading_acceptance, with the same match on refusing_check; its doc says it is the gate for a reading made with the person's corrections (read_once, queued_work). The reading.rs doc-comment scans split on 'pub fn check_reading_acceptance(' and read what precedes it (reading.rs:5052, 5504), so the new wrapper goes after it and the doc list above check_reading_acceptance gains 'then the explicit parts of the request ([`check_request_parts`])'. The refusing_check doc sentence 'Order, short-circuit and error text are those of the gate, so this adds no refusal' is reworded: 'Order, short-circuit and error text are those of the gate: check_reading_acceptance_with_corrections, and check_reading_acceptance when there are no corrections.' read_once (reading.rs:571; history in scope, second element the correction or answer that followed each earlier reading, built at reading.rs:1402-1414) passes history.iter().filter_map(|(_, c)| c.clone()). Callers of refusing_check updated: reading.rs:720 (real value), tests at reading.rs:4820, 5142, 7284, 7289, 9096; refusal_corpus.rs:1094, 1116, 1159, 1189, 1207, 1213, 2771 (Case gets corrections: Vec<String>, default empty); checks.rs:499. The parser separates prefixed lines first (split_corrections), so a correction like '1. add X' is never a part. Limits (doc comment, CHANGELOG, Risks): a retry that narrows scope in words outside the deferral list is refused until a criterion covers the part; a retried request that is itself a retry has no parts; a retried approved-work request stops at '## Source'; the re-read after a configuration change (run/pin.rs:163-164) passes no corrections.
decisions.reason: F1 from this round: the wrapper test compares the gate with refusing_check on every case and panics on a mismatch, so the gate needs a corrections-taking form and the corpus test must use it. Placing the step last keeps each existing check name; a new parameter keeps refusing_check the one function the source-order scans split on.

decisions.choice: Parser kinds. request_parts runs over the body (corrections split off) of request_own_lines with states before / in section / after. Before the heading, Enumerated parts are line-start 'N.', 'N)', '(N)', 'a)', '(a)' and inline '(1)..(2)..' or '(a)..(b)..' sequences (start at 1 or a, consecutive, 2+ markers, each followed by text with a significant stem; the last part ends at the first '. ' or line end). The Acceptance section opens on a trimmed, case-insensitive line equal to 'Acceptance:', 'Acceptance criteria:', '## Acceptance' or '## Acceptance criteria'. In the section a line starting '-', '*' or 'N.' is a Bullet with marker None (no inline scan); 'N)', '(N)', 'a)', '(a)' lines are Enumerated. Blank and indented lines stay in the section. The section ENDS at the first non-blank line with no leading whitespace that is not a list line. Marker-cited coverage and marker-based deferral or negation apply only to Enumerated parts.
decisions.reason: Bullets have no marker, so criterion 2's 'leaves (3) out ... as a follow-up' does not number bullets by position. StewardRequest puts a 'Files:' line after its bullets (steward.rs:581-585), and a later Notes list or copied block must not become required bullets. Many tests run the real gate with short dash-bullet requests and no heading; a free-form dash bullet is not a named part.

decisions.choice: Alternatives and optional parts with real introducers only. An inline Enumerated sequence is one group when (i) the text before its first marker in the same sentence holds one of ALT_INTRODUCERS ('one of the following', 'one of these', 'one of the options', 'one of:', 'pick one', 'choose one', 'choose between', 'pick between', 'either of'); or (ii) it holds 'either' and ' or ' lies before the last marker; or (iii) the last marker is directly preceded by 'or' or ', or'. Contiguous line-start parts after a non-part line holding an ALT_INTRODUCER are one group, and a part line ending ' or' groups with the next. Bare 'pick', 'choose', 'one of' or 'either' with no 'or' group nothing. A group is covered when any member is covered, skipped when every member is skipped, and the error names it. A part is optional, and skipped, when its text after the marker starts with 'optionally' or holds 'if time permits' or 'nice to have'. Groups apply to Enumerated parts only.
decisions.reason: 'Store it either as (a) a JSON file or (b) a TOML table.' must accept a reading that picks (a). Lead-ins like 'Pick up where job X left off: (1) .. (2) .. (3) ..' must stay required.

rejected.why: Ordinary lead-ins would let a reading drop two of three parts silently.

rejected.option: Treat every (a)/(b) sequence as required
rejected.why: Refuses a reading that chose one option with no honest repair.

rejected.option: Let any part containing 'or' be omitted
rejected.why: 'Add a flag or alias' would never be enforced.

decisions.choice: Stems (part_stems), word lists written once. FUNCTION_WORDS = the, and, for, not, with, without, unless, are, its, can, all, any, one, add, use, new, via, per, but, has, how, out, was, may, our, you, see, two, who, why, too, now. COMMON_WORDS = the existing list at topics.rs:157-161. PART_FILLER = pass, passes, passed, passing, cargo, clippy, fmt, content, behavior. TEXT_PATH_WORDS (dropped from part text, criterion text and paths) = crates, src, core, lib, mod, bin, rs, md, toml, yml, yaml, lock, txt. PATH_ONLY_WORDS (dropped from deliverable paths only, in addition) = tests, test, json. Steps: strip a leading [tag]; criterion text is first cleaned (drop tokens holding '/', '_' or '::', drop backtick spans starting with cargo or git, drop an unquoted span from the token cargo or git to the next of '.', ';', ',', ')' or the end; flags such as --json stay); lowercase ASCII alphanumeric words, drop all-digit words and words under 3 letters; w stripped of one trailing 's' when longer than 3 is s; drop when w or s is in FUNCTION_WORDS, COMMON_WORDS, PART_FILLER or TEXT_PATH_WORDS; cut s to 6 chars; map 'doc' to 'docume'. stems_match: equal, or the shorter has 4+ chars and is a prefix of the other. Path stems of a deliverable path: split on non-alphanumerics, drop TEXT_PATH_WORDS and PATH_ONLY_WORDS, then the same drop and stemming. Stated departure from criterion 3's wording: 'test', 'tests' and 'json' are ignored only in deliverable paths, because 'a test fails when the timeout is missing' must still cover a test part and '--json' is a real stem. Worked examples (part_stems_worked_examples): 'Add the --json flag to status' = {json, flag, statu}; 'Document the flag in the guide' = {docume, flag, guide}; 'Cover the flag with a timeout test' = {cover, flag, timeou, test}; 'Add a core test for the timeout' = {test, timeou}; 'A test fails without the change and passes with it' = {test, fail, change}; criterion '[behavior] Run cargo test -p athena-core --test timeout' = {}; path stems of crates/athena-core/tests/foo.rs = {foo}. request_parts_path_words_are_ignored pins all four lists and the departure.

decisions.choice: Coverage and error text. For each kind with 2+ parts, drop from every part the stems that occur in every part of that kind (fall back to the full set if that empties a part); n is the remaining count; need = min(2,n) for Enumerated, min(1,n) for Bullet; n = 0 is skipped. A part is covered when (a) one usable criterion, pooled with the path stems of every deliverable path whose text the criterion contains, shares at least need stems with it, or (c) a usable criterion cites the marker of an Enumerated part ('(N)', 'part N', 'item N', '(c)', 'part c'; not bare 'N)') and shares at least 1 distinctive stem. A deliverable path alone never covers. out_of_scope never covers. The error names each uncovered part (marker plus text) or group, the cause, each ignored criterion with its phrase, and says 'cover it with a deliverable and a criterion', for an Enumerated part 'or cite its marker, for example "part (3)", in a criterion that names its subject', and 'unless the request itself defers it'.
decisions.reason: Criterion 3: a path alone does not cover a part. Dropping shared stems stops a criterion for part (2) covering part (3) through a shared subject. The marker citation is the repair that always works and the reader gets one re-read (reading.rs:738-759). The tension (stricter refuses more reworded readings, looser misses dropped parts) is named in the doc comment.

rejected.option: A deliverable path alone covers, with generic path words removed
rejected.why: Lets a path cover a part with no criterion.

rejected.option: Assign each criterion to its one best part
rejected.why: More logic and tie rules than dropping shared stems.

rejected.option: Count shared words across the whole reading text
rejected.why: The summary and title echo the request, so a dropped part would look covered.

decisions.choice: Criterion-side negation scoped to a clause and the part. DEFER_PHRASES: follow-up job, follow up job, in a follow-up, in a follow up, as a follow-up, as a follow up, separate job, next job, later job, not in this job, deferred to, can wait. CRITERION_NEGATION = DEFER_PHRASES plus out of scope, out-of-scope, deferred, postponed, not done, not covered, left out, not part of. CRITERION_MARKER_NEGATION = CRITERION_NEGATION plus skipped, omitted, excluded, bare later, defer, skip, follow-up, follow up, followup, for now. negation_hit splits the criterion into clauses at '. ', '; ', ', ', ': ' and ' and ', ' but ', ' while ', ' so '. A clause is relevant when it holds a word whose stem matches a distinctive stem of the part, or (marker list, Enumerated parts only) cites the part's marker. A negation phrase in a relevant clause makes the criterion unusable for that part unless the part's own text holds the phrase; a criterion unusable for one part may cover another. The error lists each ignored criterion with its phrase.
decisions.reason: Criteria often describe refusal behaviour ('moves it to out_of_scope as a follow-up'); the phrase cancels only next to the part's own subject. 'The timeout test is deferred' cannot cover part (3); 'status lists skipped checks' still covers '(2) Report skipped checks in status'.

rejected.option: Count a phrase anywhere in the criterion
rejected.why: Cancels criteria that mention refusal in another clause.

rejected.option: A flat list where skipped, omitted and excluded cancel every criterion
rejected.why: Refuses 'status lists skipped checks'.

decisions.choice: Request-side deferral, including corrections. A part is skipped as deferred when (i) its own text holds a DEFER_PHRASES phrase, or (ii) another sentence of the request body, outside every part span, cites its marker ('(N)', 'N)', 'part N', 'item N', '(c)', 'part c', 'item c') and holds a REQUEST_DEFERRAL phrase in some clause, or (iii) a correction line (split-off prefixed lines: the current job's corrections and the retried job's corrections) has a sentence with a REQUEST_DEFERRAL phrase in a clause that cites the part's marker or shares at least need distinctive stems with the part (stem route for corrections only). REQUEST_DEFERRAL = 'out of scope', 'out-of-scope', 'for now', 'defer', 'deferred', 'follow-up', 'follow up', 'followup', and 'later' only in the forms last word of its clause, 'at a later', 'for later', 'for a later', 'come later'. skip, skipped, omitted, excluded are not request-side words. Clauses split at '; ', ', ', ': ', ' but ', ' while '. The negator guard (not, n't, never, cannot, after removing 'not in this job', 'not part of', 'not done', 'not covered') applies only to the clause holding the deferral phrase. Examples: 'Part (3) is out of scope for now; do not touch athena.toml.' defers (3); 'Part (3) must not be deferred.' does not; 'In (2), skip blank lines.' does not; 'In (2), later entries override earlier ones.' does not. Corrections: 'leave (3) for a follow-up, it is done elsewhere' defers (3); 'leave the timeout test for a follow-up' defers a part sharing {timeou, test}; 'make sure (3) is covered' does not. Stated departure from criterion 4: bare 'later' inside a part's own text ('(3) Add the dashboard later') does not defer it. 'Parts 2 and 3 can come later' cites only part 2: a stated limit.
decisions.reason: Marker citation guards against stray words; the clause-scoped negator keeps a clarifying second clause from flipping the result; criterion 4's words keep 'Part (3) is out of scope for now.' and 'Part 3 can come later.' working. The user's corrections are the one way a person defers a part after admission, so the check must not contradict them.

rejected.option: Whole-sentence negator guard
rejected.why: A later 'do not touch athena.toml' clause would leave an explicitly deferred part required.

rejected.option: Broad list (skip, skipped, omitted, excluded) on the request side
rejected.why: 'In (2), skip blank lines.' would defer a part the request wants done.

rejected.option: Narrow DEFER_PHRASES only for request sentences
rejected.why: 'Part (3) is out of scope for now.' would stay required.

rejected.option: Ignore corrections in the deferral scan
rejected.why: The check would tell the reader to cover a part the user just deferred.

decisions.choice: Measure with the producer-loop replay and state what it cannot see. loop_replay (run/mod.rs:2294-2319) runs once the change touches crates/ (touches_reading_rules, replay.rs:314); the limit is replay_limit_percent(declared) = declared 10 + 5. replay_cases (replay.rs:142-157) carries only request.text and the reading, and check_reading_text (replay.rs:54-65) passes attempt None, no referenced jobs and no corrections; athena check-reading has no corrections input. So the replay checks first-attempt requests only: a recorded retry replays as the bare text 'try again on <job>' (no parts, always accepted, which pads the denominator) and a reading accepted after a correction that deferred a part replays without that correction. The producer classifies each newly refused reading as real drop, false refusal (reworded part, deferral wording, list shape: fix the matcher, add a corpus case) or replay artifact (accepted after a recorded correction: counted separately, matcher not loosened). The report states the measured share as first-attempt only and never implies a retry or correction share. Retries and corrections are covered by corpus proxy cases and by the steward test of decision 3. Follow-ups named in the doc comment and CHANGELOG: 'replay retries with their earlier attempt and corrections' (needs check-reading to take them) and 'pass stored corrections on the re-read after a configuration change'. The declared 10% and the margin are never raised; no stored reading is edited. With no records the report says 'no replay: <reason>' and that 10% is an estimate.
decisions.reason: The 10% is an unmeasured estimate (records/ is absent from the snapshot), and a share above the limit fails the job late at the verification hold. Counting retries as accepts would make the measured share look lower than the real refusal rate.

rejected.option: Count a retried request as a replay-classified refusal kind
rejected.why: The replay never runs the retry path.

rejected.option: Raise the declared share to fit the measured result
rejected.why: Hides a matcher gap.

rejected.option: Make the replay carry attempts and corrections now
rejected.why: Changes check-reading, replay_cases and the records read, outside the deliverables.

Base reading from terms_reading (reading.rs:7293, wraps governed_reading 4635), deliverables src/status.rs and docs/guide.md, criteria '[behavior] status --json prints json' and '[content] docs/guide.md documents the flag'. Called through refuser_for (reading.rs:7288, edited to pass an empty corrections slice). Rows: (a) part 3 absent: Some('check_request_parts'); (b) part 3 only in out_of_scope as a follow-up: same; (c) criterion '[behavior] a test fails when the timeout is missing' added: None and the gate Ok; (d) '(2) Reject future timestamps' dropped: refused; (e) criterion 'Later retries reject future timestamps': accepted; (f) 'Part (3) is out of scope for this job' in the reading's criteria: still refused; (g) 'Part (3) timeout test will be added later': refused; (h) 'The timeout test is deferred': refused; (i) '(2) Report skipped checks in status' with 'status lists skipped checks': covered; (j) 'Part (2) skipped checks are omitted': ignored, error names it and 'omitted'; (k) criterion 'a reading that moves the flag to a follow-up job is refused, and the timeout test passes' added to (a): accepted; (l) 'the timeout test is moved to a follow-up job': refused; (m) deliverable tests/timeout.rs added, no criterion: refused; (n) retry: attempt = EarlierAttempt (earlier(job) at reading.rs:4382) whose request holds parts (1)-(3), current request 'try again on <job>', reading drops (3): refused; with (3) covered: accepted; (o) request has Acceptance bullets and one has no criterion: refused (Bullet). The error asserts hold 'cover it with a deliverable and a criterion' and 'cite its marker, for example "part (3)"' for an Enumerated part. Wrapper agreement (F1): the corpus test the_wrapper_agrees_with_refusing_check_on_every_case runs on every case with check_reading_acceptance_with_corrections, and a_deferring_correction_changes_the_plain_wrapper_result asserts check_reading_acceptance refuses request-parts-correction-defers-part-three while the corrections wrapper and run accept it.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core reading::tests::request_parts_refused_when_part_three_is_left_out && cargo test -p athena-core reading::tests::request_parts_retry_and_corrections && cargo test -p athena-core reading::tests::request_parts_error_names_the_part_and_the_repair && cargo test -p athena-core reading::tests::part_stems_worked_examples && cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus
demonstrations.observes: The refusing check is exactly check_request_parts for (a), (b), (d), (f), (g), (h), (l), (m), (n) without (3) and the dropped bullet; the reading is accepted for (c), (e), (i), (k) and (n) with (3) covered; the error says to cover the part with a deliverable and a criterion and to cite the marker; stem sets equal the stated ones; the wrapper test passes on every case including the correction cases.
